title: Compatibility liaison for chat conduit: OpenAI Chat Completions request/response normalization
creator: Amina Desai
description: Build a robust compatibility layer that maps OpenAI Chat Completions (v1/chat/completions) request and response shapes to Redwood's canonical chat protocol. This ticket focuses on deterministic request normalization, lossless streaming deltas, and safe function-calling plumbing so third-party clients using OpenAI semantics get predictable behavior on Redwood hosted and dedicated runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: Request mapping preserves role/name/content and metadata (message-level and top-level) with no loss for supported fields
Streaming path emits compatible delta frames that reconstruct to both OpenAI-expected and Redwood-native shapes
Function/tool calling is surfaced in the same event order as OpenAI with equivalent arguments serialization and deterministic call selection
Structured output guidance (json_schema or function return) is enforced and validation errors surfaced similarly to OpenAI error semantics
Backward-compatibility toggle allows existing Redwood customers to opt-out of strict OA semantics
End-to-end integration tests cover sync + streaming + function-calls + schema enforcement across hosted and dedicated deployments
technical_notes: Normalize incoming OA request: map 'messages' -> canonical 'chat.turns' with role mapping (user/assistant/system) and preserve 'name' field as metadata.name
Preserve top-level OA fields (temperature, max_tokens, stop) as routing metadata; translate max_tokens->max_new_tokens where applicable
Streaming: implement delta composer that emits both token and structured delta events. Include a mode flag 'oa_compat_stream' to switch between Redwood-native SSE frames and OpenAI chunk framing

Function calling: implement deterministic function selection pass in the router; when model returns a function call event, emit 'function_call' on the OA-compatible stream followed by function execution results as 'function' message
Structured outputs: validate model outputs against provided JSON Schema; when violations occur, emit an OA-like 'finish_reason' and provide 'error' details matching OpenAI error shapes where possible
Telemetry: add oa_compat.request and oa_compat.response events; attach mapping diagnostics (truncated, normalized_fields, schema_violations)
Fallbacks: if mapping requires incompatible transforms (e.g., unknown OA field), route to compatibility-transcoder which falls back to Redwood native model variant and mark in response metadata
tradeoffs: Strict OA compatibility increases surface area for edge-case bugs vs. simpler canonical mapping — mitigate by feature flag and extensive test harness
Emitting OA-shaped streaming chunks may add CPU overhead for formatting and additional metadata — acceptable for P1 customers but gated behind oa_compat_stream flag
Deterministic function selection layer can change model behavior slightly; we prefer transparent deterministic heuristics rather than opaque shadowing to keep reproducibility for customers

2026-03-05: Function call plumbing integrated with tools-sandbox; deterministic tie-breaker logic added (score > threshold, else fallback ordering)

review_feedback: PM (Ravi): prefer explicit opt-in for OA compatibility to avoid surprising behavioral changes for existing customers
